historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission authorized taking Block 332, Lots 17, 18 and 19, beside the Downtown Bowl, by eminent domain for up to $370,000, as part of a new Central City Park; in December it appointed Royston, Hanamoto, Alley and Abey, landscape architects, to prepare the park's master plan, with the Downtown Bowl to be demolished after the new year.
The Recreation and Park Commission approved the master plan for Central City Park, at the corner of Jones and Eddy Streets, presented by Robert Royston of Royston, Hanamoto, Alley & Abey.

With the first-phase contract to clear the Downtown Bowl site let, and the final plans by Royston, Hanamoto, Alley & Abey near completion after extensive community participation and help from the Police Department, a ground-breaking celebration for Central City Park was held at Eddy and Jones Streets on March 11, 1983, with Mayor Dianne Feinstein.

On the neighborhood's proposal, the Recreation and Park Commission named Central City Park the Alfred Boeddeker Neighborhood Park; Father Boeddeker had won 46 of the 70 votes cast in a naming poll run with the North of Market Planning Coalition and The Tenderloin Times.
Father Alfred Boeddeker Neighborhood Park was dedicated in May 1985, and by the end of the month was reported to the Recreation and Park Commission as the department's most heavily used facility.
